items.description: Below example how to query all OCVS inventory information from the OCI Cloud shell
commands:
for id in $(oci search resource structured-search \
    --query-text "query vmwaresddc resources where lifecycleState != 'DELETED'" \
    --raw-output --query 'data.items[].identifier | join(`\n`, @)'); do
  sddc_json=$(oci ocvs sddc get --sddc-id "$id")
  sddc_name=$(jq -r '.data."display-name"' <<< "$sddc_json")
  vmware_version=$(jq -r '.data."vmware-software-version"' <<< "$sddc_json")
  compartment_id=$(jq -r '.data."compartment-id"' <<< "$sddc_json")

  echo
  echo "=============================================================="
  echo "SDDC:                    $sddc_name"
  echo "VMware software version: $vmware_version"
  echo "=============================================================="

  clusters_json=$(oci ocvs cluster list \
    --compartment-id "$compartment_id" \
    --sddc-id "$id" \
    --all)

  for cluster_id in $(jq -r '.data.items[].id' <<< "$clusters_json"); do
    cluster_name=$(jq -r --arg cid "$cluster_id" \
      '.data.items[] | select(.id == $cid) | ."display-name"' <<< "$clusters_json")

    echo
    echo "Cluster: $cluster_name"

    oci ocvs esxi-host list \
      --cluster-id "$cluster_id" \
      --compartment-id "$compartment_id" \
      --all |
    jq -r '
      ["display-name","lifecycle-state","compute-availability-domain",
       "host-shape-name","host-ocpu-count","current-commitment",
       "billing-contract-end-date","vcf-byol-allocation-id"],
      (.data.items[] |
        [ ."display-name",
          ."lifecycle-state",
          ."compute-availability-domain",
          ."host-shape-name",
          ."host-ocpu-count",
          ."current-commitment",
          (."billing-contract-end-date" // "-"),
          (."vcf-byol-allocation-id" // "-") ])
      | @tsv' |
    column -t -s $'\t'
  done
done

items.label: OCVS Software

children.label: Is OCVS (vCenter, ESXi) on the latest versions? If not, what version are they on and what is the upgrade plan?
commands:
$results = @(
    $global:DefaultVIServer |
        Select-Object @{Name='Type'; Expression={'vCenter'}},
                      Name, Version, Build

    Get-VMHost |
        Select-Object @{Name='Type'; Expression={'ESXi node'}},
                      Name, Version, Build
)

$results |
    Sort-Object Type, Name |
    Format-Table -AutoSize

children.label: Is NSX on the latest version? If not, what version are they on and what is the upgrade plan?
commands:
# Query NSX Manager information
$nsxManager = Read-Host 'Enter NSX Manager IP address or FQDN (without https://)'
$nsxCredential = Get-Credential -Message 'Enter NSX Manager credentials'

$nsx = Invoke-RestMethod `
    -Uri "https://$nsxManager/api/v1/node/version" `
    -Authentication Basic `
    -Credential $nsxCredential `
    -SkipCertificateCheck `
    -Method Get `
    -ErrorAction Stop

[PSCustomObject]@{
    'NSX Manager' = $nsxManager
    Version       = $nsx.product_version
    Build         = $nsx.node_version
} | Format-Table -AutoSize

children.label: Has an VMware update Download Token been requested and configured in vcenter? (for license included environments download token can be requested via an OCI Support Request ticket)
children.description:
Check by going to the vcenter appliance management page on port 5480. Go to update section and click on settings. The configured repo should have an unique token in the URL, example: https://vapp-updates.vmware.com/vai-catalog/valm/vmw/[unique_token]/version.latest/

Information can also be retrieved using powershell:
commands:
# Connect to vCenter appliance / REST-style CIS API
$cisConnection = Connect-CisServer -Server $vc -Credential $cred -Force -ErrorAction Stop

# Query VCSA update policy
$updatePolicyService = Get-CisService -Name "com.vmware.appliance.update.policy" -Server $cisConnection
$updatePolicyService.get()

items.description: You can user powershell to query information from your vcenters. See below example to make an initial connection. (make sure to use powershell version 7, run command: pwsh)
commands:
# Install PowerCLI if needed
Install-Module VMware.PowerCLI -Scope CurrentUser

Import-Module VMware.PowerCLI

# Optional: use this only if your vCenter certificate is not trusted yet
Set-PowerCLIConfiguration -Scope User -InvalidCertificateAction Ignore -Confirm:$false

# Ask for vCenter FQDN or IP interactively
$vc = Read-Host "Enter vCenter FQDN or IP address"

# Ask for username and password interactively
$cred = Get-Credential -Message "Enter your vCenter / vSphere credentials"

# Connect to vCenter
Connect-VIServer -Server $vc -Credential $cred -Force

categories.title: Networking
categories.description: Network topology, VLAN configuration and management, and NSX sizing.

items.label: Check compartment(s) where the VLANs reside, are these in the same location as the VCN? If not, possibly decreased visibility
items.description: Many customer created a VCN in a separate networking compartment. When OCVS is provisioned using this VCN, the VLANs are still created in the original OCVS compartment (not is this networking compartment). The VLANs only become visible, when switching compartment while being on the VCN's VLAN page. This does not really make them easily visible.

items.label: Is a full network diagram available for the environment?
items.description:
• Should contain details on how uplink1 connects the VCN to NSX Segments
  • Are there any routes outside of the VCN from the uplink1 and vSphere/Provision VLANs
  • Definition of any additional VLANs and their purpose

items.label: Check for additional VLANs

children.label: Are all (extra) VLANs assigned to all ESXi nodes?
How are additional VLANs being managed, especially in case of Host add / replace
How are IP addresses managed in the VLAN?
Are any external access IPs defined on the VLAN? If not, why not?
Where is VLAN traffic being routed to?
children.description: Is customer aware that InterVCN routes can NOT be overrules for VLANs. So it is not possible to inject customer's own firewall between this traffic for VLANs that sit in the same VCN.

children.label: How open are the NSGs on the additional VLANs

items.description: Example to query all VLAN info via cloud shell:
commands:
oci search resource structured-search \
  --query-text "query vlan resources return allAdditionalFields" |
jq -r '
  ["display-name","vlan-tag","cidr-block"],
  (.data.items[] |
    [ ."display-name",
      (."additional-details".vlanTag // "-"),
      (."additional-details".cidrBlock // "-") ])
  | @tsv' |
column -t -s $'\t'

children.label: VSAN fault domain matching OCI's FDs or ADs
Equal balance?
Current storage usage of VSAN? Is there enough capacity in case of fault domain failure?

items.label: Block Volumes

children.label: Inventory of block volumes
Size per volume, is there good balance across multiple volumes?
children.description: VPU is per volume. Often more performance is gained, when multiple volumes are used spread across VMs.

links.text: Performance of OCI Block Volume with OCVS

children.label: How is the used VMFS storage space vs the size of the Block Volume?
children.description: Cost of block volume is per Allocated space, not consumed space.

children.label: VPU; does the VPU setting make sense?
children.description:
VPU > 30, does not impact performance per ESXi node, only the overall performance of the volume across nodes.

VPU > 50 is not supported by OCVS Service

children.label: How are block volumes managed? (Manual, custom terraform, OCVS Datastore management)
Is block volume backup or replication turned on? Does customer understand this is officially not supported with OCVS?
children.description: backup policies, auto-performance, cross-region replication are not supported by Oracle Cloud VMware Solution.

items.label: Backup

children.label: OCVS Management stack
vCenter: How is backup of vCenter server managed?
Is backup configured on the vCenter appliance?
Is vCenter protected by a 3rd party backup solution?
NSX: Is SFTP backup of NSX configuration configured, and if so, where is this stored?
VM Backup
What backup product is used to protect the VMs on OCVS?
Where are these backups stored?
If on OCI Object Storage, in what region? If in same region, is it also replicated to another region?
What network is being used for transferring the backup data? If not VLAN, has this been considered to offload NSX load?

title: OCVS Health Check
description:
Walk through the health check for Oracle Cloud VMware Solution. Choose a category below or from the top bar, set a status for each item, and record your findings in the comments. Your progress is saved automatically in this browser.

Data privacy: No health check results are sent to or stored on the server. Statuses and comments stay on your device in this browser only. To continue on another machine, use Export results and Import results from the menu. The only information sent to the server is optional feedback on checklist items, which maintainers use to improve the health check.
